37Header · where the wordmark sits, and how big

You asked to see Apple’s strict layout, with the large title on its own row under the bar buttons, and a bigger wordmark (2026-11-25). Each option shows the screen at rest and scrolled 200px. The same in all four: the wordmark and subheader scroll away, then the small 17px wordmark fades in centred on the gear’s row over the soft edge; the gear never moves. What differs: whether the large wordmark shares the gear’s row or sits on the row under it (everything below moves down 44px), and its size, 26px as locked or 34px. 34px is our hero numeral size and also Apple’s own large-title size. The Workout tab’s large title follows whichever is chosen. All four are on the Home Demo’s switches (Header and Wordmark size) to scroll yourself.

37aRejected · 37c lockedSame line · 26px (as built)

What we have. The most compact: the first card starts highest.

37bRejected · 37c lockedBelow the gear · 26px

Apple’s strict layout at today’s size. The gear has its row to itself; the wordmark starts under it, so when it scrolls away the small one appears in the row the eye already knows. Costs 44px at rest.

37c✓ LockedBelow the gear · 34px

Apple’s strict layout at Apple’s size. The wordmark clearly leads the screen. Costs about 57px at rest: the check-in and today card start lower, and the Start Workout button still sits well above the fold.

37dRejected · 37c lockedSame line · 34px

Bigger without the extra row. The wordmark and the gear compete side by side at the top, and the small wordmark appears in the row the big one sat in.

Claude’s suggestion: 37c. It is exactly Apple’s large title (own row, 34pt), the wordmark finally stands out, and the cost is one row at rest only. Owner (2026-11-25): “I think we should do 34 and probably below the gear.” Locked: 37c. Built into the Home Demo; the Workout and Progress tabs’ titles are not decided yet.

36This week · how a done day is marked

You said Home’s This week card should look exactly like Calendar (2026-11-21). One thing still differs: Home marks a done day with a tick in the moss circle (7a, locked 2026-09-26), while Calendar shows the date in the same moss circle. Everything else on the card already matches: the dashed missed day, the blue ring for today, the grey ring for a planned day, a bare date for rest. Same sample week as the Calendar Demo.

36aRejected · 36b lockedA tick, as locked (7a)

Done reads at a glance as done, without reading a number. But Home and Calendar then draw the same day two ways, and the date of a done day is the only one missing from the row.

36b✓ LockedThe date, as Calendar

The row is a strip cut from Calendar’s month: every day shows its date, and the moss fill alone says done. Exactly like Calendar, as you asked. A done day no longer has its own symbol; the fill carries it, as it already does on Calendar.

35This week · what tapping a day does, now that Calendar has changed

Home’s This week card must match Calendar. Calendar changed on 2026-11-24: a missed day stays dashed even if its session was done on another day (6a); a moved session is tagged (10a); a day card has no button and is tapped (12b); two sessions on a day are two cards, recovery on both (12b, 13b). The grid follows on its own: Monday dashed, Tuesday one tick. The open question is a tapped day. Turn 8’s revision locked an inline summary on Home with a View session button, but the Home Demo never built it: tapping anywhere on the card, days included, opens Calendar. Full screens, the same sample week as the Calendar Demo.

35a✓ LockedA day opens Calendar on that day

The card is one target. Tapping a day opens Calendar with that day selected; tapping anywhere else opens it on today. Day detail lives in one place, Home’s height never changes, and nothing on Home has to follow Calendar’s day card. What the Home Demo already does, minus picking the day.

35bRejected · 35a lockedA day opens a summary on Home

Turn 8’s inline summary, brought in line with Calendar’s card: no button, tap a summary to open the session, two sessions as two panels with recovery on both, the Moved tag. Saves a screen on a quick look. But Home grows by a card’s height on a tap, and Home then holds a second copy of Calendar’s day card to keep in step.

Module contract
Run · shows 18 to 48h after a run with no delayed rating. Program or not.
Week · shows after the week's last scheduled session, until the next week starts.
Leaves when answered, dismissed, or the window ends. Never lingers.

20Action hierarchy · proposed rules · every known case so far

12f's grey text works when it sits under a button, but on its own it reads as body text. The proposal: two roles. Primary is always a filled button, in one of three fills chosen by what the action means. Secondary is the 12f grey text and only ever appears directly under a primary. Every place Home currently has an action is listed below under this rule.

20a✓ LockedThe system · 4 styles, 5 rules
Primary · filled
Blue
The thing to do now. 50px, #659BC8.
Moss
Confirms something earned. 50px, #6CA383. Used only when a real case needs it (e.g. answering "How was your run?"). Never forced in.
Tonal
A lesser action with no other button on the card. 44px, soft fill, from 12c.
Secondary · text
Secondary
A second action, directly under a primary. 44px tap row, 14px, #8F9098, from 12f.
Rules
1 · One primary per card, at most.
2 · The fill comes from meaning: blue = now, moss = earned, tonal = lesser.
3 · Secondary text only sits under a primary. If an action stands alone, it becomes Tonal.
4 · If the whole card is tappable, it gets no button.
5 · No chevrons on buttons or secondary text.

Bar: one segment per week up to 16 weeks, one bar per block past that. Names: under each block for up to 4 blocks, a row below at 5 or more. The two rules don't depend on each other: a 12-week program with 5 blocks gets per-week segments and a names row; a 20-week program with 3 blocks gets phase bars with names under them. Four blocks is the most that fit “Hypertrophy” under its block at the narrowest realistic split; five would force it to clip.
